# Artifact Keeper 1.11.10

A maintenance release on the 1.11 line: 3 changelog entries from 3 pull requests since 1.11.9, all on the line in #5085, #5086 and #5091. Two of them bring outbound requests that ran outside the usual proxy path in line with it: **the repository `test-upstream` probe** (#5079, in #5080) and **curation sync** (#5089, in #5090) now check the stored upstream URL with the upstream URL validation and go out on each Remote's own egress route, as proxy fetches do. The third makes **the PyPI age gate's last-known-good substitute go through the scan-on-proxy gate** (#5075, in #5077), like every other distribution download of a Remote that scans on proxy. **No schema migrations** (the line stays at migration 289) and no new settings.

## What changed

- **PyPI: the age gate's last-known-good substitute is served through the scan gate** (#5075, in #5077). When the download age gate withholds a young version, a PyPI Remote answers with the newest older version it holds. That substitute used to be served through the plain proxy path. It now goes through the same scan-on-proxy gate as a requested distribution, on the direct route and for a Remote member of a Virtual repository (under the stricter-of-two policy): a stored blocking verdict refuses it with `403`, `fail_closed` withholds it with `423` until it is scanned, and `fail_open` serves it `pending`. Repositories that do not scan on proxy are unchanged.
- **The repository `test-upstream` probe reaches the upstream the way proxy fetches do** (#5079, in #5080). `POST /api/v1/repositories/{key}/test-upstream` applies the upstream URL validation before it sends anything, and a URL the validation refuses answers `400`. The probe goes out on the repository's egress route (`direct` or `explicit` proxy), so its result reflects the path real fetches take. Its `502` message, and the curation sync failure messages built from HTTP client errors, no longer include the request URL.
- **Curation sync reaches each source Remote the way proxy fetches do** (#5089, in #5090). The sweep used one HTTP client for every staging repository, so a Remote's egress setting was not applied to its index fetches and attestation downloads, and its stored upstream URL was not checked by the upstream URL validation. Each Remote now gets a client built from its own egress configuration. A Remote whose upstream URL the validation refuses is skipped with an info log, without a request, and is not marked as synced; a PyPI attestation download URL taken from the mirror's JSON is checked the same way before it is fetched.

## Upgrade notes

There is no migration and no new or changed setting. Behaviours operators may notice:

- `test-upstream` on a repository whose upstream URL the upstream URL validation refuses now answers `400` instead of trying the request, and a probe on a repository with an `explicit` egress proxy now goes through that proxy.
- Curation sync on a Remote with an `explicit` egress proxy now goes through that proxy. A manual `POST /api/v1/curation/repos/{key}/sync` on a Remote whose upstream URL is refused reports success with nothing synced, as for an upstream-filter refusal, and on a PyPI or npm Remote its pending rows stay pending instead of failing their attestation lookup.
- On a PyPI Remote that scans on proxy, a download answered with the age gate's substitute can now be refused (`403`), withheld (`423`) or served `pending`, as a direct download of that version would be.

The full entries are in the `## [1.11.10]` section of [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/artifact-keeper/artifact-keeper/blob/v1.11.10/CHANGELOG.md).
